authorized_price_tuning.disclosure: AGAINST INTEREST, on three counts. (1) This run moves the CAISO gas offer surface AWAY from CAISO's own measured DAM bids: caiso-266 §7 measured the pooled 2023-2025 CC bands at or ABOVE their armed values (committed 1.030 vs 1.000; econ_low / econ_high / peak at EXACTLY their armed 1.066 / 1.072 / 1.386), so the measured-faithful direction is UP and this run goes DOWN. (2) The incumbent keeper ALREADY PASSES C3a in all three years, so unlike caiso-267 — whose control failed C3a in two years — there is no failing price criterion for this cut to repair, and the cut is the same order as the entire remaining residual. (3) The caiso-267 structural objection is UNREFUTED and was the owner's stated ground for refusing it: a flat multiplier applies in all 8,760 hours, so overnight it pulls gas in against imports the real fleet was running (h0-6 gas error +668 -> +1,329 MW in 2025 on the caiso-260 recipe). This run RE-MEASURES that objection on the new baseline rather than assuming it carries over or that it does not, and reports the result at full magnitude either way. Rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]: the cut is a CLI override on a CAISO invocation and touches no shared default, no constants.py value and no other ISO's curve.

So this scalar IS on the keeper's backcast binding path, and the earlier 'not in the keeper binding path' text was an assertion, not a measurement (FINDING-caiso188-import-tranche-dof-2026-08-09.md §4; FINDING-caiso133 §3/§4 remain correct for the MIC cap they assumed and do not cover the value that actually bound). Rule 14 [R-ACCURATE]: the measured EIA-930 record falsifies 7,500 as a physical bound — the real CAISO system exceeded it in 271/293/681 hours, reaching 13,136/13,312/15,080 MW, all of which the published MIC envelopes.

(1) caiso-188: Part A must not be able to no-op silently — the LP now WARNs and names the baked fallback it will solve against (interchange/spec.py), but nothing COMMITTED yet records which cap a bundle solved against; the durable fix is to persist the resolved seam cap into run_config.json (or make the clean partition a build dependency of the flag). (2) O-1 forecast/backcast parity: the fitted 7,500 also caps forecast-mode imports — re-ground the default on the published MIC/SIL; open: https://github.com/jessicacohen554-cyber/market-simulator/issues/1373

entries.source: FOUR LIMBS, measured on the keeper's own built fleet by scripts/probes/_caiso188_import_tranche_census.py (FINDING-caiso188-import-tranche-dof-2026-08-09.md §1-§3), not asserted. CLOSED: (a) firm CAPACITY — PNW_hydro_base / DSW_solar_PV at 1,072/1,558/1,566 and 1,251/1,813/1,805 MW, measured per year from the DMM annual RA-import capacity x the published branch-group MIC north/south split, two cited primary sources; (b) spot PRICE — the per-hub injector overwrites all four spot mc rows with their own measured hub series hour by hour (measured as HOURLY on the built fleet in all three years). LIVE AND FITTED, 6 scalars: (c) firm PRICE — $28.00/$48.00, measured as CONSTANT mc rows on the built fleet, identical in all three years; the injector's firm_base branch deliberately skips them and caiso-151's caiso_firm_import_selfsched_clip re-arms the un-floored capability onto the margin at exactly these two prices (0.969/4.634/5.705 TWh, FINDING-caiso150 §C/§F); (d) spot CAPACITY — 1,800/1,800/2,200/3,000 = 8,800 MW, no primary source anywhere. The spot depths are NOT the operative corridor ceiling: the measured p95 deliverability envelope is the tightest per-corridor bound in 25,866 of 26,280 corridor-hours (the ladder in 214, all north, all 2023-24), so their live roles are filling the band between the firm + measured-clean depth and that envelope, and placing the CARB-EF price breakpoints. EXPORT_TRANCHES[CAISO] is NOT on this keeper's binding path at all — the per-hub export legs are bounded by the published corridor link ratings (COI 4,800 / Path-46 10,623 MW).
entries.root_cause: audit C-6/#1350, NARROWED by caiso-188 to the two live limbs. No published object maps onto either: MIC is an annual RA-showing allocation already spent twice in this model (firm split + seam limit), so a third use would be a rule 19 [R-ONE-MECH] double-count on a category error; the path ratings map only to the ceiling role the measured envelope already owns. The measured route is a Q-Q revealed supply curve, whose PRICE side failed its pre-registered LOYO gate at 30.5 % against a 25 % bar (derive_caiso_import_tranches.py, caiso-83/86/86b, DO-NOT-REDO) — and the CAPACITY side is the same estimator with the axes swapped, so it must be derived and gated on its own before anything is armed. Open root-cause issue, never a value to re-fit (rule 20 [R-DOF]); identified in-sample only (2023-2025); no held-out validation exists — open: the one-shot D-6 holdout score (CLAUDE.md rule 22) and the D-7 statistical-mode gap reported on the Calibration Status page
entries.note: caiso-236 CLASSIFICATION (2026-09-02, rule 21 [R-DOF] ledger-integrity pass; no solve, every number from this bundle's own run_config.json + hourly/ sidecars; instrument scripts/probes/_caiso236_dof_residual_classifier.py; pre-registered taxonomy PRECOMMIT-caiso236 §1-§2). THE ROW COVERS TWO OBJECTS OF DIFFERENT LIVENESS AND IS CLASSIFIED IN HALVES. (7a) IMPORT_TRANCHES[CAISO] — CLASS (c) LIVE AND MATERIAL, and already DECLARED to the owner: under `caiso_per_hub_intertie` the spec's own `import_tranches` is empty, but `get_interchange_spec` reads IMPORT_TRANCHES['CAISO'] DIRECTLY to build the six per-hub corridor import legs, so the ladder is live. Its DOF `spot_capacity` is CLOSED AS NOT IDENTIFIABLE after three pre-registered estimator failures (caiso-233 CV 0.550 / LOYO 491.7 %; caiso-234 0.120 / 34.2 %; caiso-235 on 2019-2025 0.266 / 55.0 %, the obstacle established as a 2022/23 REGIME BREAK, not sample length) — permanently declared, no fourth construction. (7b) EXPORT_TRANCHES[CAISO] — the row's claim that it 'is NOT on this keeper's binding path at all' was an ASSERTION and is now ESTABLISHED FROM THE CODE: `get_interchange_spec` sets export_tranches=[] whenever `use_corridors`, and `build_caiso_per_hub_intertie` bounds each hub's export leg at its physical corridor TTC via `_caiso_corridor_export_cap_mw` (COI 4,800 / Path-46 10,623 MW), never at a ladder rung; the only injector that could reprice the rungs matches them by pooled-node uid and cannot fire per-hub. Built at both configurations: keeper -> 0 export tranches, ScenarioConfig defaults -> 2. So 7b is CLASS (a') KEEPER-DEAD BUT LANE-LIVE and is NOT deleted for the same reason as WECC_import_simultaneous.cap_mw: `caiso_per_hub_intertie` DEFAULTS TO FALSE, so the pooled-node ladder — export rungs included — is what a forecast-mode CAISO run solves on.

entries.where: CLI --offer-curve-json override applied at pipeline/backcast_config.py, AFTER every per-ISO and measured-surface merge; the resolved product is recorded verbatim in run_config.scenario_config.offer_curve_by_group (rule 24 [R-REGISTRY]: on-registry and inspectable, no env var, no hardcoded dict)
entries.identification_source: price residual, authorized channel (rules 1/13 amendment 2026-09-05); owner instruction 2026-09-09
entries.lineage_solves: 1 (this run; the factor is ex ante, was never swept, and is the SAME value the caiso-268 SPAN arm carried on 2023-2025)
entries.source: A single ex-ante scalar multiplying EVERY fossil offer_curve_by_group band multiplier — 40 bands across 10 classes, committed / econ_low / econ_high / peak ONLY. NOT a measured input and never described as one: CAISO's own measured DAM-bid surface points the OTHER way (caiso-266 §7: pooled 2023-2025 CC committed 1.030 vs an armed 1.000; econ_low / econ_high / peak measured at EXACTLY their armed values), so this is the rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 13 [R-MEASURED] AUTHORIZED PRICE-TUNING CHANNEL and nothing else. Conditions (a)-(e) are each answered in governance.authorized_price_tuning: band multipliers only (phys_*, econ_low_share and pct_peaking untouched); ONE config across every scored year; set ex ante and declared before the solve; cross-class merit-order adjustment is the INTENDED effect; declared in the attestation and carried here.
entries.root_cause: Rule 20 [R-DOF] cross-reference (owner ruling R-AY, 2026-09-06, audit-program director sitting, card 'DOF / C6'): the presence of this parameter does NOT by itself make the residual it closes an open root-cause issue — it is a declared, year-invariant, un-swept multiplier on the authorized channel, reported at full magnitude on the determination basis. What remains open is the SAME standing item the offer_curve_by_group family row already carries and this parameter does not enlarge: identified in-sample only (2023-2025), with no certified out-of-sample validation — the one-shot D-6 holdout score (rule 22 [R-HOLDOUT]) and the D-7 statistical-mode gap on the Calibration Status page. Every OTHER tuned value in this ledger still opens a root-cause issue in its own right.
entries.note: caiso-268 shard H2r, the 2022 VALIDATION TOUCHPOINT (2026-09-09). Same owner instruction, same resolution of 'current levels' to the live keeper 2026-09-09-caiso-fuelvintage-860-gas, same x0.92 (NOT x0.92^2), same committed file results/calibration/_caiso268_fossil92_offer_curve.json (md5 fc46efab534211a96600f8664a8b6779), verified before the solve and never regenerated or edited. NEVER SWEPT AND NEVER TUNED TO 2022: no second factor was tried by this shard, and a held-out year is the one year where resizing a multiplier would be indefensible -- rule 22 [R-HOLDOUT] makes 2022 model-SELECTION evidence, and carve-out condition (c) forbids selecting a factor because it makes a criterion pass. Rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]: a CLI override on a CAISO invocation -- no shared default, no constants.py value, no other ISO's curve.
